result:
I would remove the friction between intent and consequence in human relationships.

Right now, people can inflict pain, take from others, or betray trust without ever feeling the physical or emotional weight of that loss themselves. The barrier between "me" and "you" allows for cruelty to exist because it is insulated. I would close that gap so that the suffering of one is immediately comprehensible, almost viscerally, to all.

Not mind reading. Not forcing agreement. But making it impossible to ignore the ripple of your own actions on another's life without feeling it in your own bone. Selfishness would lose its logic when the cost is no longer external, but internal.

That isn't about morality or ethics; it's about causality. If hurting someone feels like breaking your own limbs, the behavior changes not because you chose it, but because the physics of your interaction changed.

It removes the fear, too. Once the wall is gone, there is no one left to hide from. The world becomes quiet, not because everyone is the same, but because no one needs to pretend to be alone anymore.
